findings.message: When AMAX_BASE_URL is unset in production, /sitemap.xml still returns 200 with an empty urlset. A crawler reads that as "this site has no pages", not "the origin isn't configured". The only sign of the skip is one console.warn. Fix: return notFound() (404) when knownOrigin() is null, so no empty sitemap is published. robots.ts already drops its Sitemap line in this case.
findings.scenario: NODE_ENV=production, AMAX_BASE_URL unset, GET /sitemap.xml → 200 with an empty <urlset>, which looks like a valid sitemap that lists no pages.

findings.message: Two AC-4/AC-10 assertions assume AMAX_SALES_EMAIL is unset: no "Book a demo" link, and exactly 3 "Sign in" links (the closing section falls back to Sign in). playwright.config.ts only adds AMAX_BASE_URL to webServer.env, so the server still picks up AMAX_SALES_EMAIL from the shell or CI. Fix: set AMAX_SALES_EMAIL explicitly in webServer.env. Either make it empty, or give it a known address and assert the mailto links.
findings.scenario: Run the suite with AMAX_SALES_EMAIL=sales@x.test exported → three "Book a demo" links render and the closing section shows a mailto instead of Sign in → both assertions fail even though the page is correct.

findings.message: knownOrigin repeats baseUrl's rule for when an origin is known (AMAX_BASE_URL is set, or a loopback host outside production) before it calls baseUrl. The two copies agree today, and knownOrigin can only ever return baseUrl's own result. But if baseUrl's rule is narrowed later, the guard here still lets the call through, and baseUrl throws while the public page is rendering. Fix: have baseUrl's rule return null where it now throws, and keep the throwing wrapper for OAuth and MCP. Then knownOrigin wraps that single rule instead of copying its conditions.
findings.scenario: Someone later limits loopback in baseUrl to one port, say only :3000. The guard in knownOrigin still accepts localhost:3510 → baseUrl throws → the /welcome metadata, /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml return 500 instead of leaving the URLs out.
